Dear [Mr Macmillan](/person/939),
Thank you much for your kind answer.

The second set of [cameos](/book/93) is nearly all written, but the [Monthly Packet](/periodical/52) must have the first turn of them and that will take a good while - about a year at shortest.
I am afraid you think me very idle about the [Worthies](/book/80).

The truth is that my [Mother](/person/1606) has grown so infirm of late that I have less time than usual, and that time I thought it wise to spend in completing Monthly Packet Material, Cameos and a [story](/book/81) (of James I of Scotland in Captivity) that in case of being able to do no work, there might not be a stand still. I hope however to return ere long to Alexander the Great - whom I have left a full year on the Banks of the Granicus

Yours sincerely

C M Yonge


[^1]: The first volume of Cameos from English History was published in 1868, the second in 1871.
